88617.title: A tile's date range pill offers nine presets and changes only that tile
88617.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports).
  2. You are in one location (workplace) with the data below.
  3. You use a desktop browser at 100% zoom on a screen at least 1024 pixels wide (any ordinary laptop or desktop monitor).
  4. The location has invoiced work orders with clocked technician time both this month and in earlier months.
  5. Start with no tile expanded: if a tile shows its detail panel, click its View details to close it.

Setup

  • For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on.
  • For 2: to change location, click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list. On the QA site use Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 unless a later line says otherwise.
  • For 4: check: Billing Efficiency on This Month shows a percentage (not -); set it to Last 12 Months: it shows one too; then set the pill back to This Month (the dashboard remembers your choices). If this month has none, create one invoice with clocked time today: Customers > New Customer > Name > Save (for example ZZAUTOTEST Dash Customer); Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and an Asset (Add beside either if needed) > Save (if a Confirmation says the customer is over their credit limit, click Create); the New Line window opens: What Are You Doing? (any text), Add Technician = Tech ShopView, Labor Rate = EVR Travel to EVO ($100 an hour), Estimated Time 1 and Tech Time 1, tick Line Approved > Save & Close; then the Service Advisor is filled in with your name (Admin ShopView); to use another advisor change Service Advisor in the work order's left panel; clock time as the technician: in a second browser or a private window, on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Tech (this signs you in as Tech ShopView, a technician at Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 with Time Clock on); open the work order > on the line's Labor row click Start; when done click Stop > Clock Out; to make the time exact, as Admin: the three dots at the top right of the Lines tab > Timesheets (n) > edit the record's start and end (if it cannot be edited there or in Reports > Timesheet Activities, keep the real time and use the hours Timesheet Activities shows); on the line click Story (Add tech story for this line) > type a short story > Update; click Complete (if a Missing Details window asks for Mileage, enter one > Complete All Lines); click Mark Reviewed; Finance tab > Create Invoice; close the New Customer Payment window without paying (do not send or pay the invoice). If earlier months have none, no location in the list passes this check, mark the case Blocked and write in the result comment that no location has this data.
88617.custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard in the top bar.
  2. On the Revenue tile, click the blue date pill (it reads This Month).
  3. Read the list of preset names on the right of the calendar, top to bottom.
  4. Press Escape to close the calendar.
  5. Repeat the last three steps on the Billing Efficiency, Technician Efficiency, Technician Utilization and Sales by Customer tiles.
  6. Look at the pill on the At Risk Customers tile.
  7. Write down the pill text and the headline of all six tiles.
  8. On the Billing Efficiency tile, click View details.
  9. Write down the dates along the bottom of the Billing Efficiency chart and the Worked Hours of the first row of the Advisor Analysis table.
  10. Click the Billing Efficiency date pill and click Last 12 Months in the preset list (click Apply if the calendar stays open).
  11. Read the Billing Efficiency headline and its trend line.
  12. Read the dates along the bottom of the chart and the Advisor Analysis table below it.
  13. Read the pill text and the headline of the other five tiles.
88617.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Revenue, Billing Efficiency, Technician Efficiency, Technician Utilization and Sales by Customer each have their own blue date pill.
  • Every one of those five pills lists, in this order: Last 12 Months, This Year, Last Year, This Quarter, Last Quarter, This Month, Last Month, This Week, Last Week.
  • After the change the Billing Efficiency pill reads Last 12 Months and its headline is recalculated for the twelve-month window. It is a different figure from the This Month one you wrote down unless the shop's two windows happen to match; write both figures in the result comment.
  • The Billing Efficiency trend line redraws for the new window (its shape changes).
  • The expanded chart now runs month by month from the 1st of the month eleven months back to the current month (e.g. Oct 2025 to Sep 2026 when tested in September 2026), and the Advisor Analysis rows now show twelve-month hours (the first row's Worked Hours is no longer the This Month value you wrote down).
  • The other five tiles keep exactly the pill text and headline you wrote down: three on This Month, Sales by Customer on Last 12 Months, At Risk Customers on 120 Days.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9579 (Story 7, Per-Tile Date Ranges); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, Story 7. Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, screenshots of the SV-8311 build captured 2026-09-28) boards 01_Opens_After, 03_Range_After and 05_Billing_After, used for on-screen labels only.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S7-R1: “Each KPI tile and the Sales by Customer tile has its own date-range control.”
  • S7-R2: “The date-range control offers, in this order: Last 12 Months, This Year, Last Year, This Quarter, Last Quarter, This Month, Last Month, This Week, Last Week.”
  • S7-R3: “When the user changes a tile's date range, that tile's headline value updates for the new range.”
  • S7-R4: “When the user changes a tile's date range, that tile's sparkline redraws for the new range.”
  • S7-R5: “When the user changes a tile's date range, that tile's expanded chart and table update for the new range.”
  • S7-R6: “Changing one tile's date range does not change any other tile's date range.”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.

88621.title: One very high value caps the percentage axis at 200%
88621.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports).
  2. You are in one location (workplace) with the data below.
  3. You use a desktop browser at 100% zoom on a screen at least 1024 pixels wide (any ordinary laptop or desktop monitor).
  4. A one-off very high Billing Efficiency month for one advisor exists: one invoiced work order today whose Service Advisor has nothing else invoiced this month, with one labor line of 1.00 hour assigned to a technician who clocked exactly 0.25 hours on it (1.00 / 0.25 x 100 = 400%).
  5. The location also has other advisors with ordinary monthly figures under 200% over the last twelve months, so most plotted points are at or below 200%.

Setup

  • For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on.
  • For 2: to change location, click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list. On the QA site use Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 unless a later line says otherwise.
  • For 4: pick the advisor: Reports > Advisor Analysis, Date: This month: choose an advisor with no row there (your own name, Admin ShopView, if it has none). Then Customers > New Customer > Name > Save (for example ZZAUTOTEST Dash Customer); Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and an Asset (Add beside either if needed) > Save (if a Confirmation says the customer is over their credit limit, click Create); the New Line window opens: What Are You Doing? (any text), Add Technician = Tech ShopView, Labor Rate = EVR Travel to EVO ($100 an hour), Estimated Time 1 and Tech Time 1, tick Line Approved > Save & Close; then set Service Advisor in the work order's left panel to that advisor; clock time as the technician: in a second browser or a private window, on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Tech (this signs you in as Tech ShopView, a technician at Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 with Time Clock on); open the work order > on the line's Labor row click Start; when done click Stop > Clock Out; make the clocked time exactly 0.25 hours (15 minutes), as Admin: the three dots at the top right of the Lines tab > Timesheets (n) > edit the record's start and end (if it cannot be edited there or in Reports > Timesheet Activities, keep the real time and use the hours Timesheet Activities shows); on the line click Story (Add tech story for this line) > type a short story > Update; click Complete (if a Missing Details window asks for Mileage, enter one > Complete All Lines); click Mark Reviewed; Finance tab > Create Invoice; close the New Customer Payment window without paying (do not send or pay the invoice).
  • For 5: check: Billing Efficiency set to Last 12 Months > View details shows several advisors' points; then set the pill back to This Month (the dashboard remembers your choices).
88621.custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard in the top bar.
  2. Set the Billing Efficiency pill to Last 12 Months.
  3. Click View details on the Billing Efficiency tile.
  4. Hover each point and count how many read 200% or less and how many read more than 200%.
  5. Read the top label of the left-hand axis.
  6. Hover the point of the advisor seeded above for this month (it sits at the very top edge).
88621.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Most points read 200% or less (e.g. 60 of 62 points), and at least one reads above 200%.
  • The axis tops out at 200%: its highest label reads 200%.
  • The very high point is drawn clipped at the top edge of the chart (its line runs off the top), but hovering it shows its true value, e.g. 400%.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9581 (Story 9, Chart Behavior); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, Story 9. Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, screenshots of the SV-8311 build captured 2026-09-28) board 05_Billing_After (an axis capped at 200% with one line running off the top), used for on-screen labels only.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S9-R2: “When one value is far above the rest — a value above 200% while the median of the values stays at or below 200% — the axis caps at 200% so the rest of the data stays readable. The median is taken over every plotted value on the chart, pooled across all of its drawn lines rather than computed per line, counting only points that have a value; where the number of points is even it is the mean of the two middle values. When the highest value on the chart is at or below 200% the axis simply fits the data and no cap applies.”
  • S9-R2: “When one value is far above the rest — a value above 200% while the median of the values stays at or below 200% — the axis caps at 200% so the rest of the data stays readable. The median is taken over every plotted value on the chart, pooled across all of its drawn lines rather than computed per line, counting only points that have a value; where the number of points is even it is the mean of the two middle values. When the highest value on the chart is at or below 200% the axis simply fits the data and no cap applies.”
  • S9-R3: “A value drawn above the axis cap is clipped at the top of the chart but still shows its true value on hover.”

351732.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports).
  2. You are in one location (workplace) with the data below.
  3. You use a desktop browser at 100% zoom on a screen at least 1024 pixels wide (any ordinary laptop or desktop monitor).
  4. At least two technicians appear in the Technician filter on Reports > Technician Utilization, and the location has technician time this month.

Setup

  • For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on.
  • For 2: to change location, click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list. On the QA site use Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 unless a later line says otherwise.
  • For 4: check: Reports > Technician Utilization, Date: This month: the table lists at least two technicians. If not, create one invoice with clocked time: Customers > New Customer > Name > Save (for example ZZAUTOTEST Dash Customer); Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and an Asset (Add beside either if needed) > Save (if a Confirmation says the customer is over their credit limit, click Create); the New Line window opens: What Are You Doing? (any text), Add Technician = Tech ShopView, Labor Rate = EVR Travel to EVO ($100 an hour), Estimated Time 1 and Tech Time 1, tick Line Approved > Save & Close; then the Service Advisor is filled in with your name (Admin ShopView); to use another advisor change Service Advisor in the work order's left panel; clock time as the technician: in a second browser or a private window, on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Tech (this signs you in as Tech ShopView, a technician at Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 with Time Clock on); open the work order > on the line's Labor row click Start; when done click Stop > Clock Out; to make the time exact, as Admin: the three dots at the top right of the Lines tab > Timesheets (n) > edit the record's start and end (if it cannot be edited there or in Reports > Timesheet Activities, keep the real time and use the hours Timesheet Activities shows); on the line click Story (Add tech story for this line) > type a short story > Update; click Complete (if a Missing Details window asks for Mileage, enter one > Complete All Lines); click Mark Reviewed; Finance tab > Create Invoice; close the New Customer Payment window without paying (do not send or pay the invoice). and, for a second technician, create a second technician you can sign in as: profile icon > Settings > Staff > New Staff Member: a name (for example ZZAUTOTEST Tech Two), an Email you can open, Role Technician, a Department, Location = this location, Time Clock on > Save & Close; accept the invitation email and set a password and clock time with them the same way.
351732.custom_steps:
1. Click Reports in the top bar and click Technician Utilization in the left menu.
  2. Set the Date control to This month.
  3. In the Technician filter keep one technician (any technician in the list).
  4. Hover the chart's point for this month and read the percent.
  5. Read that technician's Utilization % in the table.
  6. Click Sales in the left menu, set the Date control to This month and hover this month's bar.
  7. Read the Subtotal in the table's Totals row.
351732.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The Technician Utilization chart's point for this month shows the same percent as the technician's Utilization % in the table, allowing for the chart showing whole numbers (e.g. 70% on the chart for 70.23% in the table).
  • The Sales chart's bar for this month shows the same revenue as the report for this month, allowing for the chart showing whole dollars. Write both figures in the result comment.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9583 (Story 11, Chart on the Report Page); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, Story 11. Split out of C88624. Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, screenshots of the SV-8311 build captured 2026-09-28) boards 10_sales_Hover and 13_tu_Hover (whole-number tooltips), used for on-screen labels only.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S11-R7: “The embedded chart shows the same figures as the report it sits on.”
  • S11-R7: “The embedded chart shows the same figures as the report it sits on.”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.

204097.title: Chart value axis starts at 0 unless a value is below 0
204097.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports).
  2. You are in a location (workplace) where no invoice has been created today.
  3. You use a desktop browser at 100% zoom on a screen at least 1024 pixels wide (any ordinary laptop or desktop monitor).
  4. Today, in that location, a credit was issued against an invoice from an earlier week, larger than today's sales (e.g. $300.00), so today's revenue is negative; no invoice is created today.

Setup

  • For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on.
  • For 2: to change location, click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list. Check: Reports > Sales > Date: a custom range of today only (click today twice, then Apply): the total reads $0.00. If other people invoice there today, use a quieter location.
  • For 4: Customers > a customer > Invoices tab (turn Open only off): open an invoice dated before this week; on its work order's Finance tab, the invoice's three dots > Issue Credit, and credit more than today's sales (e.g. $300.00).
204097.custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard in the top bar.
  2. Set the Technician Efficiency pill to Last 12 Months and click View details.
  3. Read the lowest label of the left-hand axis.
  4. Set the Revenue pill to Last 12 Months and click View details.
  5. Read the lowest label of the left-hand axis.
  6. Set the Revenue pill to This Week.
  7. Read the lowest label of the left-hand axis and hover today's bar.
204097.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • On the percentage chart (Technician Efficiency) the axis starts at 0%.
  • On the dollar chart (Revenue, Last 12 Months, every month positive) the axis starts at $0.
  • On This Week, today's bar is below zero (e.g. -$300.00 when there were no sales today) and the axis extends below $0 far enough to show that bar in full.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9581 (Story 9, Chart Behavior); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, Story 9. Ruling 2026-09-24 recorded in the PRD. Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, screenshots of the SV-8311 build captured 2026-09-28) boards 04_Revenue_After and 06_TechEff_After, used for on-screen labels only.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S9-R8: “Every chart's vertical axis starts at 0, on percentage charts and dollar charts alike. The one exception: when any drawn value in the selected range is below 0, the axis extends below 0 far enough to show that value in full. (@chris ruling, 2026-09-24.)”
  • S9-R8: “Every chart's vertical axis starts at 0, on percentage charts and dollar charts alike. The one exception: when any drawn value in the selected range is below 0, the axis extends below 0 far enough to show that value in full. (@chris ruling, 2026-09-24.)”
  • S9-R8: “Every chart's vertical axis starts at 0, on percentage charts and dollar charts alike. The one exception: when any drawn value in the selected range is below 0, the axis extends below 0 far enough to show that value in full. (@chris ruling, 2026-09-24.)”
